Rules / Performance

SK4002 Review iteration-local delegate captures

A lambda or anonymous delegate in a loop body captures fresh iteration-local storage.

CategoryPerformance
Default severityhint
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3

Why

Capturing a foreach iteration variable or a local declared in a loop body can create a closure environment for each iteration. The diagnostic identifies the capture, not a measured heap allocation count: compiler and JIT optimizations vary. A hot path may benefit from an explicit-state API, but hoisting or reusing the closure can change retained values and is not automatically safe.

Example

Instead of:

foreach (var item in items) { callbacks.Add(() => Use(item)); }

Write:

// If measured hot, use an API that accepts explicit state; otherwise retain the intentional captures.

When it does not fire

Only delegate-converted lambdas and anonymous methods directly nested in a for, foreach, while or do body are considered. Semantic capture must include a local declared in that body or the nearest ordinary foreach iteration variable in C# 5 or later. Captures of this, parameters, outside-loop locals and for initializer variables are excluded. Static/noncapturing delegates, expression trees and nested callable bodies are excluded. Foreach deconstruction variables and method-group conversions are outside the initial scope. Default hint is a review signal, not a claim that the loop is hot; promote it by path only after measuring. No fix is offered.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK4002.severity
